newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent jumps on Iran-Germany row, U.S. products.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent jumps on Iran-Germany row, U.S. products.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures rallied to session highs in late trade on Thursday, boosted by concerns about worsening relations between Europe and Iran and gains on U.S. refined product markets, dealers said.
May Brent crude put on 45 cents to $18.20 a barrel by 1839 GMT, just five cents off the session high and 66 cents above the low posted in early afternoon dealing.
Brokers said the combination of a row between Germany and Iran over the killing of Kurdish exiles and the closure of the Houston ship channel due to a capsized barge drove prices higher.

"The Texas closure helped push U.S. gasoline higher but the other thing people have been looking at is the recall of European ambassadors from Iran and the possible implications of that," said a broker.
Germany ordered four Iranian diplomats to leave the country after a Berlin court decision implicating Tehran in the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in a Berlin restaurant.

The European Union invited member countries to recall their ambassadors from Iran for consultations. Tehran responded by withdrawing its ambassador from Germany and expelling four German diplomats. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
